title: Experimental DFlash drafter data, training, export, and acceptance lifecycle

sources.notes: Models corpus-id deduplication, exact prompt/completion replay identity, response_start, unique cache salt, capture-file completion, retry exhaustion, and missing-record failure; HTTP/thread timing is abstract.
Models deterministic prompt identities, append-only resume, raw reasoning-preserving completions, pausing and corpus count; prompt text and sampling numerics are abstract.

Owns stage markers, minimum corpus gate, capture disk budget, service lifecycle, acceptance non-promotion, and health-only fallback. A healthy candidate suppresses the ordinary production boot; shell stage bodies have no callable symbols and are explained in the chapter.
Top-level shell harness with no named functions: validates assets, serially boots equal-context baseline/candidate arms, collects quality/ladder evidence, and invokes summarize.
Models exact feature keys, dtype/shape/layer/mask/finiteness/no-copy constraints, truncation skip, one-record-at-a-time mmap lifetime, idempotent links, and atomic manifest publication.
Models DFlash-state admission, exact training/native key sets, q/k/v shape validation and fusion, reference-config restoration, lineage ambiguity, and atomic native export.
Models aligned 120-prompt top-5 distribution evidence, JSD threshold, exact six-rung ladder validation, acceptance counters, effective-decode threshold, and pass/fail summary.

Chapter specifies exact Laguna geometry, target-hidden width/layers, context normalization, per-head softplus gate and residual structure. Tensor/attention/cache execution remains an external PyTorch/Transformers/SpecForge numerical contract.
Declarative configuration has no symbols. It pins offline target/features, 3072 window, one-GPU DFlash training, CPU optimizer offload, objective knobs, retention, and null warmstart/resume fields.
Models exact native config and 69-key schema, duplicate/incomplete shard rejection, fused-QKV dimensions, 81-key training schema, bounded shards, and atomic config/index writes.
Contract examples for feature linking/reading, normalized shapes and shared storage, mmap lifetime, mask/layer/no-copy rejection, and adapter/config window agreement; not modeled as runtime behavior.

Contract examples for config/key conversion, pilot shape, exclusive resume/warmstart, distribution comparison, inclusive boundaries and shell parsing; not evidence that live training or serving passed.
Top-level shell harness with no named functions: enforces environment/GPU exclusivity, stages data, chooses exactly one warmstart/resume override, invokes external training, then export.
Import-time entrypoint with no locally declared function: registers laguna_dflash_model, then delegates process behavior to external specforge.cli.main.
Referenced dependency used by drafter_capture for capture environment, stable filenames and request identity; hook tensor-production internals are outside this assigned inventory.
External harness invoked by acceptance.sh to produce ladder rows. The drafter model validates its observable row contract but does not model the probe implementation.

assumptions: The checked-in workflow is experimental. Accepted means its recorded quality, speculative-acceptance and effective-decode thresholds passed; no assigned source promotes the checkpoint into the ordinary production recipe.

The target HTTP service, hidden-capture hook, filesystem atomic rename semantics, systemd, PyTorch, Transformers, safetensors, Hugging Face snapshot resolution, SpecForge and the decode-ladder producer are external boundaries.
A final capture filename denotes the hook's completed atomic record write; the driver does not inspect tensor contents before the adapter stage.

The Reyu model collapses worker retries, locks, service boots, training, tensor conversion and file publication into stage actions while retaining observable counts, identity, schemas, masks, shapes and error branches.
Text-to-token replay may differ from originally sampled token ids at rare completion merge boundaries because datagen stores text rather than completion ids.
Adapter success can contain zero usable records when every supervised suffix falls outside max_length; external training, rather than adapter validation, must then fail or refuse useful work.

The external training state is treated as trained only after SpecForge exits successfully and produces the exact DFlash state schema required by export; optimizer and attention numerics are not inferred from configuration.

The supervisor's fallback is health-based rather than identity-based: a healthy candidate is preserved without ordinary production restoration, while a failed ordinary boot after no healthy endpoint remains an operator-required state.

A nonzero acceptance command leaves the acceptance marker absent and the candidate unshipped, but drafter_overnight.sh can still reach its explicit final exit 0; evidence/marker state, not supervisor status alone, carries the decision.

implementation_checks.description: CPU: construct the small tensor record used by test_adapter, then independently corrupt dtype, [T,6,3072]/[T,18432] shape, suffix mask, layer ids, finiteness and shared storage; require valid admission and specific rejection of each corruption.

CPU/filesystem: stage usable plus prompt-truncated records, read manifest totals and SpecForge normalized shapes, confirm links share source files, and separately show that an all-truncated input is accounted as a zero-record manifest rather than rejected.
CPU/filesystem: provide duplicate ids and malformed/non-text JSONL; confirm first-occurrence deduplication and fail-closed structural validation without contacting a server.
CPU: feed the exact Poolside config and one-field mutations; compare architecture/type/target-layer transformation and require rejection of every geometry or capture-point mismatch.
CPU: split a synthetic fused tensor of shape [11264,3072], confirm q/k/v shapes [9216,3072], [1024,3072], [1024,3072], and compare concatenation to the source; reject an incorrect fused shape.
CPU: fuse a complete synthetic training dictionary against the native key schema, compare key consumption and QKV ordering, and require failures for missing, extra or wrong-shaped projections.
CPU/filesystem: exercise direct state, single latest lineage, multiple latest lineages, step fallback and empty-directory branches to compare exact checkpoint identity selection.

CPU: compare identical and perturbed 120-row top-logprob evidence, including unlisted tail probability, and verify prompt/schema/depth misalignment is rejected rather than paired by position silently.
CPU: validate the six ordered contexts and mutate counters, percentages, label, timing finiteness and order one at a time; each malformed evidence case must fail closed.
CPU: compare inclusive 108/120 quality, 60% aggregate/every-rung acceptance and 6.0 ms/token boundaries with immediately below/above cases; inspect the emitted decision JSON and return status.

CPU/source inspection: instantiate or validate the mapped config and mutate each geometry, layer layout and dflash_config field; this checks framework admission only, not attention numerical parity or GPU training.
Source inspection: confirm the resume branch contains only training.resume_from and the fresh branch only model.draft_checkpoint_path, matching pilot.yaml where both defaults are null.

Source inspection: trace success, stage-error, signal, acceptance-failure and fallback-failure exits; show that a healthy candidate prevents the ordinary production boot and distinguish that state from recipe promotion and supervisor exit status.
